Text.Text: You came back with the rhythm still under your skin. Good. Keep practicing the restraint we spoke of. Don't let anyone sell you hunger and call it Blood Frenzy.
Your hands are still chasing the kill. Reach rank 50 in Vibroblade, then come back. I need you ready to learn what happens after the blade stops.

Blood Frenzy starts below Veles, in the Viscara Sewers Depths. Six Red Vein Scavengers have my codex down there. They're treating its warnings as instructions. Put the six down and bring it back. Then we'll talk about why your breath matters after a kill.
Take this key into the Veles sewers and find the Sewers Depths entrance. Six scavengers, then the codex back to me here on the Trade Concourse. Read the warnings if you have time.
The six Red Vein Scavengers are in the Sewers Depths. Bring their codex here to the Trade Concourse. I don't want another pupil learning it backward.
That binding. Hm. They read the warnings and kept only the appetite. At least the book came home before it learned their stink.
Credits for the hazard. Spend them on repairs, not celebration. The lesson starts with timing, not rage.

Pulse-Frame Training Droids are hammering my old cadence into anyone who listens down in the Sewers Depths. Five of them. Break their drill and bring me the pulse metronome. Kess's circle is learning patience, and I don't trust what they'll use it for.
Count thirteen beats. On the thirteenth, the opening is yours. Bring the metronome core back intact; if it still clicks, it can still teach.
Five Pulse-Frame Training Droids in the Sewers Depths. Break them and bring me the pulse metronome. I'll show you what that cadence was meant to teach.
Hear that tiny skip? That is where a patient blade wins. Most duelists mistake that silence for mercy. It is not.
Keep the metronome in your head, not your pack. Your hand moves after the beat, never before it.

The next lesson stinks of stim smoke. The Blood Frenzy Butcher has turned the rhythm into a chemical leash. Challenge him in the Sewers Depths and bring me his adrenal glass when he's dead. I need to see what he's been putting into people.
Use the challenge marker in the Sewers Depths to call the Butcher. Take help if you need it. The glass comes back here; his mixtures stay down there.
Call the Butcher at the Sewers Depths challenge marker. Kill him and bring me the adrenal glass. Don't try his work on yourself.
Clotted, overcooked, ugly. This is what happens when discipline rots and someone mistakes a syringe for a teacher.
Hazard pay. And a warning: if your pulse starts asking for orders, stop listening.

Now we make restraint you can hold. Four Blood Frenzy Duelists in the Sewers Depths carry fragments of the charm Kess broke. Defeat the four and bring those fragments to me. They won't need them to keep another recruit in his circle.
Four fragments. No trophies, no speeches. Bring them back before their school finds a new throat to shout through.
Four Blood Frenzy Duelists in the Sewers Depths. Beat them and bring me their charm fragments. The glass is ready for the binding.
Good. These pieces remember restraint better than their owners did. That is sad, useful, and common.
Now I can bind the lesson. The next cut is the one that matters.

Kess Draavo calls himself the Blood Frenzy King. He teaches the breath after a kill as hunger. You'll find his challenge marker in the Cistern Ring, beyond the Sewers Depths. Call him and end it. Then come back here. There's a last part I want you to hear from me.
The Cistern Ring is beyond the Sewers Depths. Use its challenge marker to call Kess. Keep your breath your own, whatever he tells you to do with it.
Kess waits in the Cistern Ring. Call him at the challenge marker, kill him, then return to the Trade Concourse. Your lesson doesn't end with his last breath.
I felt the rhythm stop from here. Either Kess is dead, or the whole undercity learned discipline at once. I know which one I believe.
Kess is dead. Let yourself breathe before you reach for the next fight. When you're ready, I'll teach you Blood Frenzy properly: what to do with the heat of victory before it spends you.
Sera taps two fingers to her wrist. 'The body celebrates before the mind catches up. Blood Frenzy teaches you to spend that surge, not become it. Victory gives heat; discipline gives it a shape.'
'Red Vein' was a name thieves used when they wanted murder to sound like scholarship. They stole an old copy, stripped out every warning, and left scavengers under Veles to read the leftovers aloud.

In the Veles sewers, find the entrance marked for the Sewers Depths. It opens for the key holder. If you bring allies, gather them close before you step through. I'll give you the key when you take the work.
'Because rage lies about time. It says now, now, now. The thirteenth beat teaches waiting while your nerves burn. The Pulse-Frames punish anyone who swings early.'
'A timing core, old Republic training stock before Veles learned to hide its better mistakes. Do not crack it open. If it still clicks when you hand it to me, it can teach you more than any corpse.'
'He turned the after-kill rush into a chemical leash. A stim tap in the arm, an audience stupid enough to clap, and suddenly discipline becomes a show with a body count.'
'Blood, stim resin, adrenal salts, heat. It hardens in the lab equipment when the mixture is abused. Ugly, useful. I can make it say stop when your pulse says again.'
'Because sometimes the hand needs an object before it believes an order. Not forever. Just long enough to remember the blade belongs to you, not the moment after the kill.'
'Kess has them performing around fragments like relics. Every duelist thinks the next kill proves devotion. Take the fragments before devotion becomes recruitment.'
'Clever enough to learn the lesson, vain enough to rename the wound. He calls himself king because teacher would make him answer for what he made.'

The refusal. That's what I used to call it. Your body wants to spend everything after a victory. You learn to keep that heat, give it a shape, and choose where it goes. Kess never learned to stop choosing the next kill.
'Count the breath after a kill. If you need another target before that breath is done, you are not using Blood Frenzy. It is using you.'
I'm listening. Give me the first cut.
I recovered the Red Vein Codex.
The codex is still below Veles.
The codex is yours. The warnings are still in it.
I will break their rhythm.
I brought the pulse metron.
The droids are still keeping time.
The metronome core still ticks.
The Butcher falls.
I have the adrenal glass.
The lab is not finished.
The Butcher is dead. I brought the glass.
I will take the fragments.
I recovered the charm fragments.
The duelists still hold the fragments.
I have the charm fragments.
I will end his circle.
Kess is still breathing.
Kess is dead. His circle is quiet.
Not now.
What is Blood Frenzy, really?
Why is the Red Vein Codex in the Sewers Depths?
How do I reach the Sewers Depths?
Why the thirteen beats?
What is the pulse metronome?
What did the Butcher do to the lesson?
What is adrenal glass?
Why make a restraint charm?
What are Kess's duelists doing?
Who is Kess Draavo?
What happens after he dies?
What should I keep practicing?
